Big <MATH_0001>-categories.
In many texts a <MATH_0002>-category is allowed to have a class of
objects (but hopefully a ``class of classes'' is not allowed).
We will allow these ``big'' <MATH_0003>-categories as well, but only
in the following list of cases (to be updated as we go along):
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> The <MATH_0004>-category of categories <MATH_0005>.
<STRUCT_0003> The <MATH_0006>-category of categories <MATH_0007>.
<STRUCT_0004> The <MATH_0008>-category of groupoids <MATH_0009>;
this is a <MATH_0010>-category.
<STRUCT_0005> The <MATH_0011>-category of fibred categories over a fixed category.
<STRUCT_0006> The <MATH_0012>-category of fibred categories over a fixed category.
<STRUCT_0007> The <MATH_0013>-category of categories fibred in groupoids over a fixed category;
this is a <MATH_0014>-category.
<STRUCT_0008> The <MATH_0015>-category of stacks over a fixed site.
<STRUCT_0009> The <MATH_0016>-category of stacks over a fixed site.
<STRUCT_0010> The <MATH_0017>-category of stacks in groupoids over a fixed site;
this is a <MATH_0018>-category.
<STRUCT_0011> The <MATH_0019>-category of stacks in setoids over a fixed site;
this is a <MATH_0020>-category.
<STRUCT_0012> The <MATH_0021>-category of algebraic stacks over a fixed scheme;
this is a <MATH_0022>-category.
<STRUCT_0013>
See Definition <REF_0001>.
Note that in each case the class of objects of the <MATH_0023>-category
<MATH_0024> is a proper class, but for all objects <MATH_0025>
the category <MATH_0026> is ``small'' (according to
our conventions).
